people.x: Identified as the Qianlong emperor who became Retired Emperor after the Jiaqing 1 seal-bestowal and planned inner abdication in Qianlong 60.
Individuated only as the heir for the planned Qianlong 60 inner abdication; personal name not stated in this chunk.
The First Teacher temple dedicatee is Confucius; the Qianlong-era ritual dates the sacrifice, not his lifetime.

translationRepairs: That same year the emperor instructed the ritual officials that since the investiture ceremony would not be held, there was no need to prepare the full ceremonial regalia, whose manufacture would take considerable time.

That same year the emperor instructed the ritual officials that since the ceremony for investing the crown prince would not be held, there was no need to prepare the full ceremonial regalia, whose manufacture would take considerable time.
冊立皇太子典禮 explicitly names the ceremony as the crown prince's investiture; restoring that object removes the English ambiguity.
The Defender-general of the State's ceremonial guard comprised one dark-apricot umbrella, one blue fan, and six flag-spears.
The Defender-general of the State's ceremonial guard comprised one apricot-yellow umbrella, one blue fan, and six flag-spears.
The next three sentences explain that the former golden-yellow umbrella was changed to an apricot-yellow one. 杳黃 is a copying or encoding error for 杏黃, not a color called dark apricot.
Defender-general of the State ceremonial guard: one dark-apricot umbrella, one blue fan, and six flag-spears.
Defender-general of the State ceremonial guard: one apricot-yellow umbrella, one blue fan, and six flag-spears.
The literal field should follow the explicit revision at s0260 and render the umbrella 杏黃, apricot-yellow.
A prince's primary consort ranked with a Princess of Imperial Title, except that her curved-handle umbrella was red; four maidservants accompanied her at court.
A prince's primary consort ranked with a Princess of the First Rank, except that her curved-handle umbrella was red; four maidservants accompanied her at court.
The proposal correctly identifies a title inconsistency, but Princess of the First Rank is the standard rendering already used throughout Qingshigao 102, 103, 114, and 166 for 固倫公主.
A prince's primary consort was accorded the same as a Princess of Imperial Title; only the curved-handle umbrella used red, with four attending maidservants at court.
A prince's primary consort was accorded the same as a Princess of the First Rank; only the curved-handle umbrella used red, with four attending maidservants at court.
Use the established corpus rendering Princess of the First Rank for 固倫公主 rather than either inconsistent phrase in this chapter.

Ceremonial guard for imperial sons-in-law: an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of Imperial Title received two red staffs, one red umbrella, two large and small blue fans, ten flag spears, and two leopard-tail spears.

Ceremonial guard for imperial sons-in-law: an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of the First Rank received two red staffs, one red umbrella, two large and small blue fans, ten flag spears, and two leopard-tail spears.
固倫公主 is Princess of the First Rank in the surrounding Qing institutional chapters; the revised wording restores that established title.

Ceremonial guard for imperial sons-in-law: for an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of Imperial Title, two red staffs, one red umbrella, two large and small blue fans, ten flag spears, and two leopard-tail spears.

Ceremonial guard for imperial sons-in-law: for an imperial son-in-law of a Princess of the First Rank, two red staffs, one red umbrella, two large and small blue fans, ten flag spears, and two leopard-tail spears.
The literal field should use the same established Princess of the First Rank title for 固倫公主.
